summary: Account is brand new (19 total followers). Instagram bio violates brand rules: names niches (hotels, cafes, gyms, homestays), region (Himachal), promises 24hr delivery, offers free site check in bio. Reels lose 77% viewers in first 3s. Lead_gen outperforms chatbot 3:1 per reach. Question hooks lead (1.75x), mistake angles lead (1.46x). Zero real engagement on LinkedIn.
guidance:
- Rotate to **question** or **mistake** hooks (top performers); pause contrast hooks (0.23x of top3).
- Avoid repeating "morning search" or "scrolling fatigue" framings — already used.
- Write as a developer showing real work, not an ad. No demos, no client claims, no guarantees.
- Use bright-desk or silhouette images (1.5x).
- Focus on universal problems: repeated basic queries, manual lead hunting, inconsistent info — relatable to any Indian small business.

instructions.research: Find 3 real Indian small-business owners (any city, any sector) discussing on LinkedIn/Instagram how they lose time answering the same WhatsApp questions daily. Screenshot anonymized quotes for writer.
instructions.analysis: Compare the last 3 chatbot posts (Nov 2, 8, 12) — note which phrasing got any saves/shares. Flag any repeated words to avoid today.
instructions.writer: Draft a question-hook post: "What happens to incoming WhatsApp enquiries while you're with a walk-in customer?" Keep it under 130 words. End with: "Pay after you approve. DM for a quick chat on whether a chatbot fits." No demo offer.
instructions.image: Create a bright-desk style static image: split screen — left side a busy counter, right side a simple chat bubble flow labelled "Example: auto-reply to common questions". No logos, no client names.
instructions.video: Skip video today. Reel retention is 77% drop at 3s; static image matches current best image style (bright-desk 1.53x).

manual_tips: Update Instagram bio to: "AI chatbots, animated ads, lead lists & websites for small businesses across India. Pay after approval. DM for honest advice." Removes niche, region, timeframe, and bio free-offer violations.
Comment thoughtfully on 5 posts by Indian freelancers/agencies discussing lead-gen pain points — use 'Freelancers' or 'Agencies' language, not 'web developer'.
Reply to the 1 comment on your best chatbot post (Nov 2) with a genuine follow-up question to keep conversation going.
